summary: This Docker Compose configuration defines two services: a Joomla web application running on FrankenPHP and a MySQL database. The Joomla service exposes ports 80 and 443, connects to the database using environment variables, and stores its files in a named volume. The database service uses MySQL 8.2 and persists its data in a separate volume.

explanations.4: This specifies which Docker image to use for the Joomla service—in this case, a hardened version of FrankenPHP (a PHP runtime) with Joomla pre-configured for MySQL.
explanations.7: The %% symbols are placeholders that get replaced at runtime; this maps port 80 on your computer to port 80 inside the container so you can access the web server.
explanations.11: This tells Joomla where to find the database server—'db' is the hostname of the other service defined below in this same Compose file.
explanations.16: A named volume is like a persistent folder that survives even if the container stops; here Joomla's files are stored so they don't disappear when you restart.
explanations.17: This ensures the Joomla service waits for the database service to start before trying to connect to it.
explanations.30: This section defines the named volumes referenced above—Docker will create and manage these storage areas automatically.
